source.method: straight-line fit to the published characteristic curve over one log H window shared by all three channels, [-2.54, -0.64], on Fujifilm's printed lux-second axis, anchored at the sheet's printed ISO 200/24° through the ISO 5800 speed point (green and the slower of red and blue, each at minimum density plus 0.15), which sits 0.33 log H (about 1.1 stop) faster on that axis than ISO 200 predicts, a shift of +0.34, which makes the window Kodak's [-2.2, -0.3]

name: Fujifilm 200
note: Dye gammas are this stock's own, read off its maker's published characteristic curve. Nothing here is measured from a roll. It used to be an alias of Kodak Gold 200, which rested on Fujifilm's first sheet of December 2021, since withdrawn. The current sheet, AF3-0261E of February 2022, prints a different curve, so it has its own profile. Fujifilm's sheets print lux-seconds, but their ISO 5800 speed points do not sit where Kodak's do, so the window is anchored at the printed speed like every sheet not on Kodak's footing.
